text:
THE DUENNA (rapturously):
  Oh, look! The knocker is wrapped in cloths! . . .
  (To the knocker):
  They have gagged you so that your metal
  Would not disturb the fine speeches—you little brute!
  (She lifts it with infinite care and knocks softly.)

ROXANE (seeing that the door is being opened):
  Let us go in! . . .
  (From the threshold, to Cyrano):
  If Christian comes, as I presume he will,
  Have him wait for me!

CYRANO (quickly, as she is about to disappear):
  Ah! . . .
  (She turns around):
  On what, according to your custom,
  Do you intend to question him today?

ROXANE:
  On . . .

CYRANO (quickly):
  On?

ROXANE:
  But you will keep silent about it!

CYRANO:
  Like a wall.

ROXANE:
  On nothing! . . . I shall say to him: Go on! Give yourself free rein!
  Improvise. Speak of love. Be splendid!

CYRANO (smiling):
  Good.

ROXANE:
  Hush! . . .

CYRANO:
  Hush! . . .

ROXANE:
  Not a word! . . .
  (She goes inside and closes the door again.)

CYRANO (bowing to her once the door is closed):
  With thanks to you.
  (The door opens again and Roxane puts her head out.)

ROXANE:
  He might prepare himself! . . .

CYRANO:
  Devil, no! . . .

BOTH TOGETHER:
  Hush! . . .
  (The door closes.)

CYRANO (calling):
  Christian!



Scene 3.IV.

Cyrano, Christian.


CYRANO:
  I know everything that is needed. Ready thy memory.
  Here is the opportunity to cover oneself with glory.
  Let us lose no time. Do not look so sullen.
  Quickly, let us go back to thy house; I am going to teach thee . . .

CHRISTIAN:
  No!

CYRANO:
  Eh?

CHRISTIAN:
  No! I am waiting for Roxane here.

CYRANO:
  What madness
  Has seized thee? Come quickly and learn . . .

CHRISTIAN:
  No, I tell thee!
  I am weary of borrowing my letters, my speeches,
  And of playing this part, and of always trembling! . . .
  It was fine at first! But I feel that she loves me!
  Thank thee. I am no longer afraid. I shall speak for myself.

CYRANO:
  Indeed!

CHRISTIAN:
  And who tells thee that I would not know how? . . .
  I am not so stupid, after all! Thou shalt see!
  But, my dear fellow, thy lessons have been profitable to me.
  I shall know how to speak alone! And, by all the devils,
  I shall always know how to take her in my arms! . . .
  (Catching sight of Roxane, who is coming back out of Clomire’s house):
  —It is she! Cyrano, no, do not leave me!

CYRANO (bowing to him):
  Speak on your own, sir.
  (He disappears behind the garden wall.)



Scene 3.V.

Christian, Roxane, some précieux and précieuses, and the duenna,
for a moment.


ROXANE (coming out of Clomire’s house with a company from whom she
  takes her leave, with curtsies and bows):
  Barthénoïde!—Alcandre!—Grémione! . . .

THE DUENNA (despairingly):
  We missed the discourse on Tenderness!
  (She goes into Roxane’s house.)

ROXANE (still bidding farewell):
  Urimédonte! . . . Farewell! . . .
  (They all bow to Roxane, bow again to one another, part, and
  move away along different streets. Roxane sees Christian):
  It is you! . . .
  (She goes to him):
  Evening is falling.
  Wait. They are far away. The air is mild. Not a passerby.
  Let us sit down. Speak. I am listening.

CHRISTIAN (sits near her on the bench. A silence):
  I love you.

ROXANE (closing her eyes):
  Yes, speak to me of love.

CHRISTIAN:
  I love thee.

ROXANE:
  That is the theme.
  Embroider, embroider.

CHRISTIAN:
  I . . . you . . .

ROXANE:
  Embroider!

CHRISTIAN:
  I love thee so much.

ROXANE:
  Of course! And then?

CHRISTIAN:
  And then . . . I would be so happy
  If you loved me!—Tell me, Roxane, that thou lovest me!

ROXANE (pouting):
  You offer me gruel when I was hoping for creams!
  Tell me a little how you love me? . . .

CHRISTIAN:
  Why . . . greatly.

ROXANE:
  Oh! . . . Unlabyrinth your feelings!

CHRISTIAN (having drawn closer and devouring the fair nape of her neck with his eyes):
  Thy neck!
  I would like to kiss it! . . .

ROXANE:
  Christian!

CHRISTIAN:
  I love thee!

ROXANE (trying to rise):
  Again!

CHRISTIAN (quickly, holding her back):
  No! I do not love thee!

ROXANE (sitting down again):
  That is fortunate!

CHRISTIAN:
  I adore thee!

ROXANE (rising and moving away):
  Oh!

CHRISTIAN:
  Yes . . . I am becoming stupid!

ROXANE (dryly):
  And that displeases me!
  As it would displease me if you became ugly.

CHRISTIAN:
  But . . .

ROXANE:
  Go and gather up your fleeing eloquence!

CHRISTIAN:
  I . . .

ROXANE:
  You love me, I know. Farewell.
  (She goes toward the house.)

CHRISTIAN:
  Not yet!
  I shall tell you . . .

ROXANE (pushing open the door to go inside):
  That you adore me . . . yes, I know.
  No! No! Go away!

CHRISTIAN:
  But I . . .
  (She shuts the door in his face.)

CYRANO (who returned a moment ago without being seen):
  It is a success.



Scene 3.VI.

Christian, Cyrano, the pages, for a moment.


CHRISTIAN:
  Help!

CYRANO:
  No, sir.

CHRISTIAN:
  I shall die if I do not regain
  Her favor this very instant . . .

CYRANO:
  And how the devil can I
  Teach you this very instant? . . .

CHRISTIAN (seizing his arm):
  Oh! There, look, see!
  (The balcony window has lit up.)

CYRANO (moved):
  Her window!

CHRISTIAN (shouting):
  I am going to die!

CYRANO:
  Lower your voice!

CHRISTIAN (very softly):
  Die! . . .

CYRANO:
  The night is dark . . .

CHRISTIAN:
  Well?

CYRANO:
  It can be repaired.
  You do not deserve it . . . Stand there, wretch!
  There, in front of the balcony! I shall place myself beneath it . . .
  And I shall prompt thee with thy words.

CHRISTIAN:
  But . . .

CYRANO:
  Be quiet!

THE PAGES (reappearing at the back, to Cyrano):
  Hey!

CYRANO:
  Hush! . . .
  (He signals to them to speak softly.)

FIRST PAGE (in a low voice):
  We have just serenaded
  Montfleury! . . .

CYRANO (softly, quickly):
  Go and lie in ambush,
  One at that street corner, and the other at this one;
  And if some troublesome passerby comes this way,
  Play a tune!

SECOND PAGE:
  What tune, Monsieur Gassendist?

CYRANO:
  A merry one for a woman, and for a man, a sad one!
  (The pages disappear, one at each street corner.—To Christian):
  Call her!

CHRISTIAN:
  Roxane!

CYRANO (picking up pebbles, which he throws at the windowpanes):
  Wait! A few pebbles.



Scene VII.

Roxane, Christian, Cyrano, at first hidden beneath the balcony.


ROXANE (partly opening her window):
  Who is calling me?
